He might not be a bad person, but he is a horrible instructor. He constantly says how he took this course over his predecessors, so he cannot change the syllabus etc., but then he adds additional information randomly. He acts as if this is the only course we are taking instead of treating this course as what it is: a course to teach engineering majors some economics terminology. His calculations look too complicated, but they all come from very basic formulas in reality. His thought system is hard to understand, and he is unwilling to change. Studying by yourself would make much more sense. He criticizes the book, but the book is far more understandable than him! He says he has no control over the TAs, which is weird since he is the coordinator of this course. He also thinks every section needs to have the same GPA, which is not the case for other IE courses. His accent is generally not a problem, but there are some words he mispronounces. Also, for the final exam, he said he might ask "hard" questions, which is again weird that an instructor focuses more on asking "hard" questions instead of asking questions that determine the student's understanding of the course.
TL;DR: Do not take this course from him if he doesn't change!

He is a good person and tries his best to teach. Yet, he is not very good at reading, and is unaware of the fact that there is more than one way to write an LP constraint. Furthermore, he grades in a binary fashion, and does not care about whether the answer makes sense or scientifically correct; he only checks if it is EXACTLY the same with the one in his answer sheet. This may be right for deterministic answers involving arithmetic calculations to reach a number, but is simply WRONG to grade this way for constraints that are written in a correct, but different way.
